Welcome to the Glitch in the Matrix Rules/FAQ

Some rules (In progress)

  • Glitches should be witnessed first hand, or told to you by a trusted family member, unless you have an article/video that you think everyone must know about.

  • This is a place for outrageously strange happenings, deja vu to the extreme, and the physically impossible.

  • Self posts are highly recommended, as images that do not contribute to the story directly will probably get the post removed.

  • No Rage Comics

  • If you feel your post has been removed unfairly, please message the mod(s). Normally we respond in a fair amount of time, and will be happy to help you out with any problems.

  • Keep the stories as true as you are aware, /v/nosleep is for your inner ghost story teller ;)

  • No abusive posts, or back talking mods if they ask you to refrain from a particular activity

  • "I had a dream, and it came true"

-If you start off with this, it better be something remarkable, or along the lines of dream-sharing. If it's mundane then let's not bother, shall we?

-Mundane being something like "I dreamed that I would see a kid on a road, then I drove past a school and saw a kid on the road! Guise it's a glitch!" NO! ಠ_ಠ

  • NO PICTURES OF TEXT (NO!)

  • Deja Vu IS allowed, but once again, avoid the mundane. It's always neat when something small happens but in all likelihood it is just a trick of your brain ;)

  • Think you can explain what REALLY happened in a glitch report? Feel free to try!

-The Paranormal does not necessarily indicate a glitch, and may not be appropriate here. Glitches tend to be physics related, or time related. Not ruling out "seeing" something, but think before you post!

-No Ouija boards, sorry but they aren't a glitch. They're bullshit.

-No Aliens, not a glitch.

-No psychics, unless they called themselves the oracle and gave you cookies.

-Is it a ghost story? /v/nosleep is the place for it. :)

  • Blacking out is not a glitch, unless it happened to a group of people and everyone was sober.

  • Precognition, it better be amazing, not just imagining walking down a street and later gasp you did!

  • Driving alone and feeling the car "teleport" forward a few yards may not be a glitch, it is all too easy to be tired, or not paying attention during a drive. A carload of Ivy-Leaguers going to college twice is interesting, however.

  • When I was a young child... stop. Due to the way human memory works, one can easily confuse dreams or fantasies with reality. Think before you post, there have been excellent stories, but most of them are obviously childhood confusion.

The FAQ's

Q: Is this place for creepy stories? A: Not quite, but they will probably freak you out! Scary stories are for /v/nosleep, stuff about creepy people and ghosts tend towards /v/letsnotmeet

Q: Dude, this place is totally blowing my mind here's my story A: Uhh, well, you're probably just stoned! :) We support the freedoms of others, but if in all likelihood you just ate the bag of chips instead of it disappearing into a wormhole then.... you probably did!

Q: My new post isn't showing up! A: It's either been caught in the spam filter or removed. Send the moderator(s) a message and we'll look into it as soon as possible.

Creating A World Without Money: Sharehaus Berlin

Money is the root of all evil, of course. But, the idea of "money" also solves a problem. A physical dollar is just worthless paper. But the idea of a dollar allows for global electronic commerce.

You couldn't have stores like Amazon with just barter. There needs to be some sort of generic agreed-upon store of value (fungible assets). You may be an excellent painter but, what if Amazon doesn't want paintings? They want something that takes up minimal space, can be sent electronically, and holds a constant value.

The idea in the video is great for a small village or group of people who all know each other. I like gardening and you like making beer -- we can trade with each other. But, this model doesn't scale up beyond a few hundred people. Cities of millions of people would not be able to function on a barter system alone.

Most cultures tend to revert back to precious stones and metals to store value if there is no fiat currency. Fungibility is an important aspect of the idea of money.

(Fun fact, there are more key space in Serpent/AES256 than there are atoms on Earth.) Though there are rumors about XAES which is assumed to be 1024 bits encryption, it probably not necessary anytime in the future considering the size of available keyspace.

Hey Atko, one of the problems with reddit is that with 10-20 mods on all the major subs, there are hundreds of users who are well-positioned to curate content as they see fit. If this site ever becomes big and a PR firm figures out how to get ahold of one or two key spots in a major subverse, they could effectively use that subverse to shape public perception by curating content as they see fit.

I've thought about this problem quite a bit, and I have some ideas I'd like to bring up with you:

I think that whatever eventually becomes reddit's successor needs to limit the problem of "powermods." This could mean imposing a limit of no more than one default subverse per user, but it would be better to get rid of moderators altogehter. The job of tagging and removing inappropriate submissions could be done by group consenseus instead.

For instance, with a good coder, you could create a system wherein users tag submissions that they think should be removed. If the number of users who tag a submission for removal reaches some threshold (say, 50% as many removal tags as upvotes, and at least 50 removal tags overall) then the submission would be removed. It would then be up to the admins to decide if the post should go back up, but the initial "moderation" would be done by the community itself.

In addition to "tagging for removal," you could have similarly user-voted flair that wouldn't actually remove the article--things like "False/May be misleading"; "out of date"; etc.

To minimize content manipulation by sock accounts, you could perhaps even edit the code to make it so that users can't log into a new account more than once every half hour (I'm not a coder, so I don't know how feasible that last part is, but it's something worth thinking about).

In any event, thank you for creating this site and I hope it becomes what reddit could have been if it hadn't sold out to the dark side (i.e.; become a PR playground).

Again, their "hands off" approach is a mechanism to ensure plausible deniability and nothing more.

If one bot was created that submitted all community-driven removals to a specific sub that users could keep track of, and another bot noted the username of the admin removing a post and the username of the post's OP, then I think you'd basically be set (you wouldn't want the content to show up with this bot, however, since presumably the reason the submission was taken down is because it violated a site-wide rule). Curious users could go to the userpage of the OP and see what they'd submitted, but the violating post would no longer be visible elsewhere.

That's as close to a purely democratic and transparent process as I can currently conceive.
